Once buffers are placed in the system, Start the ROBOFISH_user_program.py program by pasting the below command in an Anaconda command prompt: python ROBOFISH_user_program.py Enter "all" to update the experimental information. This will open Notepad++ wih the system info file. Edit the information with all experimental metadata under Parameters. Screenshot example of the info file with experimental metadata. Give the names of the buffers connected to the various ports. Port numbers and buffer names Then fill in the volumes of the buffers that were placed in the system. Screenshot example of the info file with buffer volumes. Fill in the codes of the hybridization mixes. The code is C<chamber number>_<round number>. So chamber one hybridization round 6 is "C1_06". Screenshot example of the info file with hybridization numbers. Optionally add the names of the genes or detection probe code to the Targets. The System will take this information and put it in a round specific info file that will be placed with the images, so that downstream the targets and images can be matched. Screenshot example of the info file with the round targets. In this example Round 1 will contain 5 genes in different channels of the microscope. "Cux2" is labeled with a green probe and is imaged with the FITC channel. Screenshot example of the info file with the round targets. This is the codes we use for barcoded EEL experiments. The 1 or two indicates the bit location in the brcode. After saving and closing the info file, and pressing enter in the ROBOFISH_user_program, a pop-up will open where you can tick the boxes of new buffers that need to be primed. Screenshot example of the priming tickbox. In this case the Washbuffer (WB) and Imaging buffer (IB) will be primed. (Only prime newly connected buffers and never prime hybridization mixes!)

steps.title: Clean ITO Slides
steps.instruction: Clean ITO slides through a series of sonication steps using aluminum foil to cover the beakers.

substeps.instruction: Submerge slides in Acetone and sonicate for 00:20:00 on high power.
Discard Acetone, submerge in 2-Propanol, and sonicate for 00:20:00 on high power (replace sonicator water if warmed).
Discard 2-Propanol, submerge in dH2O, and sonicate for 00:20:00 on high power (replace sonicator water if warmed).
Discard dH2O and replace with fresh dH2O; store slides in water for at least a couple of days (use within one month).

steps.title: Dry Slides
steps.instruction: Place slides in a rack and let them dry; optionally use compressed air or nitrogen gas to remove large droplets.

steps.title: Prepare Functionalization Solution
steps.instruction: Prepare a coating solution in a dedicated glass staining jar under an inert nitrogen gas environment.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 300 mL of 2% volume GPTMS ((3-Glycidyloxypropyl)Trimethoxysilane) in anhydrous acetone.
Place the jar in a box/bag with steady nitrogen gas flow.

steps.title: Functionalize Slides
steps.instruction: Coat the slides with the GPTMS solution and wash.

substeps.instruction: Submerge the rack of slides in the functionalization solution for 02:00:00 under nitrogen atmosphere.
Pour out the GPTMS mix and wash slides with acetone, then discard the acetone.
Dry the slides with nitrogen gas.

steps.title: Spot Poly-T Solution
steps.instruction: Apply Poly-T spotting solution to the conductive side of the ITO glass.

substeps.instruction: Identify the conductive side using a multimeter set to resistance.
Add 40 µL of Poly-T spotting solution.
Incubate for 01:00:00 at 25 °C under a 24x24mm plastic coverslip (Hybrislip - Grace biolabs).
Optionally mark the coating area with a solvent prove marker (e.g., Moist Mark Plus).

steps.title: Remove Coverslip and Wash
steps.instruction: Carefully remove the plastic coverslip and wash the coated area.

substeps.instruction: Place a few drops of SSC 2X on the edge of the coverslip; wait for it to move under the slip, then lift the corner with forceps.
Wash the slide 5 times with SSC 2X by pipetting onto the coated area and aspirating from a corner.

steps.title: Block Epoxy Groups
steps.instruction: Block remaining epoxy groups at room temperature.

substeps.instruction: Apply 60 µL of 0.1 Mass/% volume Poly-D-Lysin in dH2O for 00:30:00 (do not use a coverslip).
Wash 3 times with dH2O.

steps.title: Final Slide Preparation
steps.instruction: Prepare the slide for tissue capture.

substeps.instruction: Pipette off the bead mixture from a corner of the coated area.
Let the slide air dry, avoiding residue in the capture area and avoiding touching the surface.

steps.title: Tissue Capture and Storage
steps.instruction: Apply a tissue cryosection to the slide and store.

substeps.instruction: Make a 10 µm cryosection of the tissue sample and catch it on the capture area of the slide.
Let dry for a few minutes.
Place in a container (e.g., petri dish) to prevent frost accumulation and store at -80 °C.

steps.title: Reference Marking
steps.instruction: Mark the tissue section for later alignment.

substeps.instruction: Thaw the section.
Make two reference crosses on either side of the tissue section on the back side using a solvent prove and non-fluorescent marker pen (e.g., Moist Mark Plus).

steps.title: Nuclear Staining
steps.instruction: Stain the nuclei of the sample.

substeps.instruction: Stain for 00:05:00 with 1 ug/ml Propidium Iodide in SSC 2X.
Remove the top coverslip, gasket, and SSC 2X.

steps.title: Electrophoresis Assembly
steps.instruction: Assemble the electrophoresis sandwich using ITO slides and PDMS spacers.

substeps.instruction: Attach a short wire to the sample ITO coverslip (Anode) and a clean uncoated ITO slide (Cathode) using conductive copper tape.
Place the sample slide in the EEL holder and secure the wire in the slit.
Place two 1.5 mm thick PDMS strips on either side of the sample.
Cover with the top electrode (conductive side facing sample) and secure the wire in the slit.
Optionally place a weight on top to keep slides stacked.
Connect the sample slide to the positive pole (Anode) and the top electrode to the negative pole (Cathode).
Pipette electrophoresis buffer between the glasses.

steps.title: Perform Electrophoresis
steps.instruction: Apply voltage to the assembly for a set duration.

substeps.instruction: Set power source to 10 Volts/cm (or 1.5V if using a 1.5 mm PDMS spacer) and electrophorese for 00:20:00.

steps.title: Disassemble Electrophoresis Setup
steps.instruction: Carefully remove the sample from the electrophoresis holder.

substeps.instruction: Turn off power, disconnect wires, and remove electrophoresis buffer with a paper tissue.
Remove the sandwich from the EEL holder and place on a flat surface.
Carefully remove the top electrode and PDMS spacers.
While pushing the capture slide onto a flat surface, remove the wire and copper tape using horizontal force to avoid breaking the glass.
Place the glass in a petri dish.

steps.title: Post-Electrophoresis Washing
steps.instruction: Wash the sample to remove SDS and salts.

substeps.instruction: Wash 3 times for 00:05:00 with 5% SDS in SSC 2X at 30 °C (pre-warm the solution).
Wash 5 times with SSC 2X.

steps.title: Prepare Probe Hybridization Mix
steps.instruction: Prepare the probe stock solution using a Speed Vac.

substeps.instruction: Dry the probe stock solution in a low binding Eppendorf tube using a Speed Vac.
Dissolve in 20 µL of 30% formamide hybridization mix.
Ensure probes are hybridized at 1 nanomolar (nM) per individual probe (e.g., 1000 nM total for 1000 probes).

steps.title: Hybridization Incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate the slide with the hybridization mix in a humidified environment.

substeps.instruction: Place a paper tissue in a petri dish, wet with SSC 2X, cover with parafilm, and place two spacers on top.
Place the slide on the spacers and remove as much liquid from the slide as possible.
Add the hybridization mix (avoiding bubbles) and cover with a plastic coverslip (Hybrislip, Grace Biolabs).
Close the petri dish and place paper towels on top to prevent condensation.
Incubate for at least 40:00:00 at 38.5 °C.

steps.title: Remove Hybridization Coverslip
steps.instruction: Safely remove the coverslip after incubation.

substeps.instruction: Take the slide out of the incubator.
Place SSC 2X on the edge of the plastic coverslip and wait until adsorbed before removing.

steps.title: Bead Application
steps.instruction: Apply Europium doped beads to the slide.

substeps.instruction: Mix Europium doped beads small (200nm) and big (1um) in a 1:333 ratio in dH2O.
Place ~100 µL on the slide, ensuring full area coverage.
Incubate for 00:03:00.
Wash 5 times with 200 µL SSC 2X.

steps.title: Sample Sealing
steps.instruction: Seal the tissue section and reference crosses.

substeps.instruction: Cut a gasket out of parafilm and place it around the tissue section and reference crosses.
Close with a 24x32mm glass coverslip (or fitting size).
Add sufficient SSC 2X to ensure no air bubbles are present on the tissue or crosses.
Drain excess SSC 2X from the side with a paper towel.

steps.title: Initial Imaging and Point Generation
steps.instruction: Generate imaging coordinates for nuclei and RNA signals.

substeps.instruction: Take a low power (10X) overview image.
Generate Point_set_1 for RNA signal imaging using a high power objective (60X).
Generate Point_set_2 for nuclei imaging using a medium power objective (40X).
Image nuclei using Point_set_2 (ensure beads are imaged for alignment).
Using the high power objective, add the locations of the 4 armpits of the reference crosses to Point_set_1 and save.

steps.title: Pre-Flow Cell Washing
steps.instruction: Wash the sample before mounting.

substeps.instruction: Wash 5 times with TBE 1X.

steps.title: RNA Fixation
steps.instruction: Fix the RNA in the sample.

substeps.instruction: Fix for 00:10:00 with 4% PFA in 1X PBS.
Wash 5 times with SSC 2X.

steps.title: Flow Cell Mounting and Priming
steps.instruction: Mount the slide in the flow cell and connect to the fluidics system.

substeps.instruction: Mount the slide in the flow cell and place on the microscope stage.
Connect to the fluidic system, outlet to waste bottle, and connect temperature control cables/hoses.
Prime the chamber with SSC 2X using a syringe via the manual prime port.

steps.title: Fluidics and Detection Cycle
steps.instruction: Run the automated detection cycles via Jupyter lab and ROBOFISH software.

substeps.instruction: Start Jupyter lab, verify folder paths, and start the scheduler for detection cycles.
Wash 4 times (15 minutes each) with 30% formamide wash buffer at 47 °C.
Wash 4 times with SSC 2X.
Manually inject 1ml of 4% PFA in 1X PBS; fix for 10 minutes at 22 °C.
Manually wash with >5ml of SSC 2X at 22 °C.
Hybridize for 10 minutes with fluorescent probes at 37 °C.
Wash 3 times (3 minutes each) with 20% formamide washing buffer at 37 °C.
Wash 4 times with SSC 2X at 37 °C.
Set temperature to 22 °C and inject imaging buffer.

steps.title: Imaging and Coordinate Correction
steps.instruction: Perform imaging and correct coordinates using reference crosses.

substeps.instruction: Correct Point_set_1 using the reference crosses by aligning the current image with the previous image of the cross.
Save corrected Point_set_1 and start imaging (following the Nikon NIS Elements Job or custom software reading the Start_imaging_file).
Set perfect focus on the surface before imaging.

steps.title: Repeat Labeling Rounds
steps.instruction: Repeat the labeling and imaging process for additional rounds.

substeps.instruction: Wash 4 times with SSC 2X at 22 °C.
Hybridize for 10 minutes with fluorescent detection probes at 37 °C.
Wash 3 times (3 minutes each) with 20% formamide washing buffer at 37 °C.
Wash 4 times with SSC 2X at 37 °C.
Set temperature to 22 °C and inject imaging buffer.

steps.title: Fluorophore Stripping
steps.instruction: Strip fluorophores and prepare for the next cycle.

substeps.instruction: Wash the slide twice with dH2O.
Incubate the sample for 00:05:00 in 6X SSC.
Wash the sample two times with 2X SSC.
Strip fluorophores 2 times (10 minutes each) with stripping buffer at 22 °C.
Wash 6 times with SSC 2X.
Image the signal.
